parsed.headline: Israeli Defense Minister alleges Syrian President is waiting for Netanyahu's election defeat to resume attacks on Druze communities

pages.text: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz stated on Thursday that Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa is waiting for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to lose Israel's election before resuming attacks on Druze communities in Syria, according to the North Press Agency. parsed.headline: Israeli settlers attack Palestinian olive farmers and Washington Post journalist in West Bank

pages.text: On October 15, 2026, masked Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians harvesting olives in the occupied West Bank, injuring several people including a Washington Post photojournalist. In the town of Abu Falah, near Ramallah, witnesses reported that approximately 80 settlers, some carrying clubs, firearms, or gas canisters, descended from a hill to confront villagers. The settlers used slingshots to hurl rocks and set fire to olive trees and cars. Witnesses stated that when Palestinians picked up rocks to defend themselves, the Israeli military arrived in jeeps and fired tear gas in the direction of the Palestinians. One witness reported seeing an armed settler fire a gun, and another reported a Palestinian man being shot in the thigh by Israeli soldiers. The Palestinian Red Crescent Society reported at least six people were injured in Abu Falah, while a local official stated 12 Palestinians were injured, including four dual Palestinian-American citizens. The Israeli military did not immediately respond to a request for comment regarding the incident. 12

parsed.headline: Ghana National Research Fund to prioritize local solutions for national challenges

pages.text: The Ghana National Research Fund (GNRF) intends to prioritize research into food security, environmental protection, health care, and technological innovation to address development challenges and reduce dependence on external research funding, according to officials in Accra. The announcement was made by Professor Marian Dorcas Quain, the Deputy Director-General of the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), and Professor Shamsudin Ziblim, the Deputy Administrator of the Ghana Research Fund, during a Scientific Conference and Innovation Fair 2026. Speaking on the topic of “Research Funding and Implementation in Ghana,” Professor Quain stated that the country requires a coordinated research system focused on practical solutions and specific challenges. The fund is expected to support researchers working on home-grown solutions, such as climate-smart crop varieties, sustainable natural resource management, emerging diseases, and innovations in science, technology, and engineering.

Professor Quain noted that investing in agricultural research is essential for improving food production, strengthening food security, and developing seeds capable of withstanding changing weather conditions to increase yields. Regarding environmental protection, Quain said the fund would support research into sustainable natural resource management, specifically addressing environmental damage caused by illegal mining, known as galamsey. The fund will also support health-related research to assist scientists in responding to emerging diseases. Additionally, Quain indicated that investment in STEM, ICT, and engineering is necessary to stimulate innovation, while research in the humanities and social sciences could provide evidence-based solutions to economic development, corruption, and other societal challenges.

parsed.headline: Ghana to host signing of UN trade convention on October 26, 2026

pages.text: Ghana is scheduled to host the signing of the United Nations Convention on Negotiable Cargo Documents, referred to as the Accra Convention, on October 26, 2026. The convention aims to modernize trade documentation and improve the efficiency of international commerce by establishing a legal framework for negotiable cargo documents in both paper and electronic formats for goods transported via road, rail, air, and sea. During a media engagement organized by the Ghana Shippers’ Authority (GSA) in Accra on October 15, 2026, Stella A. Ansah, the Director of the Foreign Trade and Negotiations Directorate at the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, announced the event on behalf of sector Minister Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare. The engagement was intended to sensitize the media to the significance of the convention and Ghana’s role in hosting the ceremony. The signing is expected to involve representatives from governments, international organizations, and the global trading community. Professor Ransford Edward Gyampo, the Chief Executive Officer of the GSA, noted that modernizing trade documentation is a response to increasing digitalization and complex global supply chains.

parsed.headline: Trump calls Ukraine’s renewed strikes on Russian oil refineries ‘a disgrace’

pages.text: U.S. President Donald Trump has called Ukraine’s renewed strikes on Russian oil refineries “a disgrace” and criticized Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy following the collapse of an energy ceasefire. Trump stated that Zelenskyy is “more difficult to deal with than [Russian President Vladimir] Putin.” The criticism follows Ukraine's decision to resume attacks on Russian oil infrastructure after Zelenskyy announced Kyiv was abandoning a ceasefire unilaterally declared by Trump on October 11, 2026. Ukraine had briefly halted its attacks to demonstrate readiness for peace talks, but Russia had continued its strikes on Ukrainian power plants. Tensions between Washington and Kyiv have escalated over a deal made by the U.S. president to import diesel from Moscow and curbs on Ukraine's battlefield satellite network. Zelenskyy, speaking at an EU summit in Brussels, said he could not accept the diesel deal because a gas agreement could follow, stating, “If I don't stand up to this... who else will?”

During the EU summit in Brussels, Zelenskyy addressed the need for funding to help Ukraine through its fifth winter since the 2022 Russian invasion. He told the European Council that the war will cost €155bn (£131bn; $174bn) next year, noting that at least €70bn is required from the EU for defense and weapons. Zelenskyy also stated that while Ukraine has the capacity to produce up to three times more drones, the country lacks sufficient money for that production. Arriving at the summit on Friday, Zelenskyy expressed that it was good to be back among allies, referring to EU leaders as “real leaders.”

parsed.headline: Bangladesh health division orders medical libraries to stock books on Zia and Khaleda

pages.text: The Health Services Division (HSD) in Bangladesh has directed all government and private medical colleges and hospitals to keep three specific books in their libraries, according to a directive issued on September 27. The books include two works by Mahfuz Ullah, titled “President Zia: Rajnoitik Jiboni” and “Begum Khaleda Zia: Jibon O Songram,” which focus on late president Ziaur Rahman and former prime minister Khaleda Zia, respectively, and “Sobar Agey Bangladesh,” listed as a book by Tarique Rahman. 1. The HSD directive instructed heads of all agencies under its jurisdiction to take necessary steps. The Directorate General of Nursing and Midwifery has since directed its subordinate organisations to comply with the order. 2. The decision followed an August 23 application from Jatiyatabadi Prokashona Sangstha, a publisher represented by Zahir Deepti. The publisher requested that the books be purchased and preserved in medical libraries, describing them as historical documents regarding the political history of Bangladesh that are important for medical professionals and citizens. 3. State Minister for Health MA Muhit reportedly “strongly recommended” the proposal on the application, which included his seal and signature. When contacted on October 15, 2026, Muhit declined to comment on the matter. 4. This directive follows a previous attempt to place the same three books in government primary-school libraries. While the primary and mass education ministry issued such an order on June 3, the ministry cancelled that decision on July 6.

parsed.headline: Four people killed and two burned while fighting wildfires in Indonesia's Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park

pages.text: At least four people died and two others suffered severe burns while battling wildfires in the Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park in East Java, Indonesia, officials said on Friday. According to a Forestry Ministry statement, the victims were trapped by fast-spreading flames and thick smoke during what the ministry described as the country's worst wildfires in a decade. Jules Abraham Abast, a spokesperson for the East Java police, stated the victims were part of a 12-member firefighting team composed of local volunteers, members of the community fire brigade, and national park personnel. The ministry noted that the incident highlights the high-risk nature of forest and land fire extinguishing operations. By the evening of October 15, 2026, the number of satellite-detected hotspots in Indonesia had reached 799, an increase from 372 the previous day, though officials noted that not all hotspots necessarily represent individual fires.
